items.q: Mitral stenosis with an enlarged left atrium in sinus rhythm often shows what P wave?
o: Broad notched P in lead two called P mitrale
items.exp: Slow atrial conduction in a big atrium widens and notches the P, which mirrors the echo enlargement. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left atrial enlargement.

items.q: Longstanding mitral stenosis with a huge atrium most often ends in which rhythm?
items.exp: Stretched fibrotic atria sustain fibrillation, so echo size tracks the rhythm risk directly. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on atrial consequences.

items.q: Severe aortic stenosis often shows which ECG pattern?
items.exp: Thick pressured walls raise voltage with repolarisation strain, matching the echo wall thickness. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular hypertrophy.

items.q: Chronic severe mitral regurgitation with volume overload often shows what?
o: Left ventricular hypertrophy with a volume pattern
items.exp: Eccentric cavity growth raises lateral voltage, which mirrors the echo dilatation. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on chamber consequences.

items.q: Chronic severe aortic regurgitation often shows what?
o: Left ventricular hypertrophy with volume overload pattern
items.exp: Longstanding leak dilates and thickens the ventricle, so voltage grows with the echo cavity. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on chamber consequences.

items.q: Severe tricuspid regurgitation with a big right atrium may show what P wave?
o: Tall peaked P called P pulmonale
items.exp: High right atrial pressure peaks the P early, which mirrors the echo atrial enlargement. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right atrial enlargement.

items.q: Large pericardial effusion classically shows what voltage pattern?
items.exp: Fluid dampens surface potentials, so small complexes accompany the echo free space. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on pericardium.

items.q: Beat to beat alternation of QRS height with a large effusion suggests what?
o: Electrical alternans from a swinging heart
items.exp: The heart swings within fluid so the axis alternates, which pairs with echo motion of the same swing. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on pericardial effusion.

items.q: Anterior infarction with apical akinesia on echo often leaves what ECG mark?
o: Pathological Q waves with poor R progression
items.exp: Dead anterior muscle loses R force, so Q waves map to the akinetic echo segments. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on wall motion assessment.

items.q: Ostium secundum atrial septal defect often shows which conduction pattern?
items.exp: Right volume load delays right activation, so the rSR pattern mirrors the echo right enlargement. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on septal defects.

items.q: Pulmonary hypertension on echo with right hypertrophy may show what axis?
items.exp: Right mass pulls forces rightward, matching septal flattening and raised jet velocity on echo. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on pulmonary hypertension.

items.q: Tall right precordial forces with deep S laterally in a young adult fit what echo finding?
o: Right ventricular hypertrophy from pressure load
items.exp: Dominant right forces mean right muscle bulk, which the echo measures as wall thickness. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right ventricular hypertrophy.

items.q: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may show which striking ECG sign?
o: Giant negative T waves in lateral leads
items.exp: Apical bulk repolarises late, so deep T inversion mirrors the echo apical thickness. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on hypertrophy patterns.

items.q: Dilated cardiomyopathy with poor function often shows what conduction mark?
o: Broad QRS with left bundle pattern
items.exp: Diffuse slow conduction widens the QRS, matching the weak dilated echo pump. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on chamber size and function.

items.q: Atrial fibrillation with a fast rate in mitral stenosis raises the gradient because of what?
o: Short diastole with loss of atrial kick
items.exp: Less filling time with no atrial push drops output while the fixed hole holds gradient high. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on heart rate effects.

items.q: Ventricular paced rhythm widens the QRS and desynchronises the ventricle. What echo effect may follow?
o: Lower ejection fraction with dyssynchronous walls
items.exp: Uncoordinated activation wastes contraction, so echo shows late walls with a lower pump. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on dyssynchrony.

items.q: Low voltage with sinus tachycardia and a large effusion with collapse fits what physiology?
items.exp: Fluid pressure blocks filling while damping voltage, so fast rate compensates a squeezed echo heart. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tamponade signs.

items.q: Right bundle disease with left anterior fascicular delay after infarction suggests what?
items.exp: Two fascicles down after anterior injury warns the last path may fail, while echo maps the scar. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on infarct assessment.

items.q: Left anterior descending artery occlusion injures which echo walls?
items.exp: The vessel feeds the front and septum, so those echo segments fail together with anterior ECG injury. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on coronary territories.

items.q: Right coronary artery occlusion injures which echo wall?
items.exp: The right vessel feeds the inferior wall, so inferior echo defects match inferior ECG injury. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on coronary territories.

items.q: Left circumflex occlusion injures which echo wall?
items.exp: The circumflex wraps to the side wall, so lateral echo defects match lateral ECG injury. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on coronary territories.

items.q: Left main occlusion threatens which echo picture?
o: Extensive anterior and lateral failure with shock
items.exp: The trunk feeds most of the left ventricle, so widespread failure with shock follows. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on coronary territories.

items.q: Why does left atrial enlargement in mitral disease predict atrial fibrillation?
o: Stretch and fibrosis split conduction into reentry
items.exp: Big fibrotic atria sustain circus movement, so echo atrial size tracks rhythm risk. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left atrial enlargement.

items.q: Why does severe aortic stenosis produce strain pattern ST depression?
o: Thick muscle outgrows supply with high wall stress
items.exp: Hypertrophy with systolic load starves the subendocardium, so strain mirrors echo thickness and gradient. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on pressure overload effects.

items.q: Why does pericardial fluid lower ECG voltage?
o: Fluid insulates and distances the heart from electrodes
items.exp: A fluid rim damps potentials at the skin, so low voltage matches the echo free space. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on pericardium.

items.q: Why does hyperkalaemia style peaked T differ from ischaemia in echo correlation?
o: Echo walls move normally without regional defect
items.exp: Metabolic T changes lack a wall motion defect, so a normal moving echo points away from infarct. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on wall motion assessment.

items.q: P pulmonale in tricuspid disease reflects which echo measure?
items.exp: Peaked P tracks right atrial load, which echo grades by volume and cava plethora. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right atrial enlargement.

items.q: LVH voltage on ECG with normal echo walls suggests what next step?
o: Recheck leads, body size and echo quality before labelling disease
items.exp: Voltage is sensitive but not specific, so echo truth with lead review decides rather than voltage alone. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular hypertrophy.

items.q: New left bundle branch block with anterior wall failure on echo suggests what?
items.exp: Fresh LBBB with matching anterior defect marks a large proximal lesion needing urgent care. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on infarct assessment.

items.q: Atrial flutter with 2 to 1 conduction in mitral disease risks what echo finding?
o: Left atrial thrombus from slow appendage flow
items.exp: Organised atrial stasis still clots, so appendage velocities and thrombus are checked as in fibrillation. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on atrial consequences.

items.q: Poor R progression across chest leads with apical thinning on echo means what?
items.exp: Lost anterior forces with a thin bright apex mark old infarct scar rather than simple lead position. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on scar assessment.

items.q: Right axis with tall R in V1 and deep S in V6 in a breathless young adult fits what echo check?
items.exp: Right dominant ECG forces demand echo pressure and size study of the right heart. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right ventricular hypertrophy.
